title.narrative: Multisector human. assistance to drought affected malnourished communities in the areas of nutrition, water, health

description.narrative: Development Objective / Overall Goal: Improved survival for drought-affected communities in the Umerkot district of Sindh province, Pakistan.Specific Objective: Improved health and nutrition situation of drought affected household with Pregnant and lactating woman PLWs and children Under five years from selected villages in two (2) Union Councils of Umerkot District during the lean period.

The Sindh Province in Pakistan is at high risk for drought. Especially the district Umerkot is affected. Government data indicates that 31,390 families in Umerkot will be at high risk due to a lack of access to health facilities and food and drinking water during the upcoming lean period (May to August 2019). WHH began its humanitarian response in January 2019 with 230,000 euros of its own funds, to reach 3,500 households. This AA-funded project would allow WHH and its partner, TRDP, to fulfil the objective of meeting the immediate needs of an additional 13,300 malnourished families affected by drought in Umerkot through multisectoral emergency aid.

The project will provide relief to children under 5 years and Pregnant and Lactating women (PLW) plus small growers affected by the drought. The total covered population of the project is 13,300 families (93.100 individuals) of 200 communities in two Union Councils i.e. Faqeer Abdullah and Kaplore. The project aims to have 1.00 households or 7.00 individuals (3,080 children, 1,960 women and 1,960 men) reach food security through conditional cash transfers (conditionality of participating in the awareness sessions).Medical camps will be organized in 200 villages and transport vouchers will be distrusted to 13,300 individuals (PLW and children under 5) to access health facilities.1,000 households will be provided with vouchers to access safe water for three months, 13,300 individuals (PLW/Care givers) will participate in sessions on nutrition and WASH awareness for behavioral change and 1,000 household will received hygiene kits (7000 individuals; 3080 children, 1960 women and 1960 men).
